questions.q: What does the Contains Roles field on a sys_user_role record actually do?
options: It deletes the roles listed inside it
It restricts a role to a single named user
It has no functional effect; it's a documentation field only
It lists other roles that this role inherits — anyone granted the containing role gets everything the contained roles grant
questions.explain: Role inheritance through Contains Roles means granting one role can implicitly grant everything the roles it contains would grant.

questions.q: How does this lesson's role design discipline connect back to Delegated Administration?
options: Delegated Administration's least-privilege idea — grant the minimum needed, nothing more — is the same principle applied generally to all role assignment
It doesn't connect — Delegated Administration is unrelated to role design
Delegated Administration recommends granting the admin role to all delegates
Delegated Administration only applies to field-level ACLs, not roles
questions.explain: Delegated Administration was a specific case of least privilege; this lesson generalizes that same discipline to role design as a whole.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend building a narrow custom role instead of defaulting to a broad out-of-box role like admin or itil_admin?
options: Because out-of-box roles no longer exist in current ServiceNow versions
Because itil_admin and admin are deprecated and will be removed
A narrow role can be described in one sentence and is actually auditable, while broad OOB roles grant far more than most jobs need
Because custom roles are required by ServiceNow licensing
questions.explain: A role you can describe in a single sentence is a role you can actually audit; broad OOB roles bundle access most people assigned them never need.

questions.q: What is role sprawl, as described in this lesson?
options: A single role that contains too many fields
An accumulation of overlapping custom roles built up over time, making it hard to audit who can actually do what
The automatic expansion of a role's permissions over time with no admin action
A ServiceNow licensing term for exceeding a role quota
questions.explain: Role sprawl happens when narrow roles pile up over years with overlapping Contains Roles chains and no periodic review, making the whole hierarchy hard to audit.

questions.q: What tradeoff does this lesson identify as the real cause of role sprawl?
options: ServiceNow forces admins to create a new role for every single task
Custom roles are always less secure than out-of-box roles
Role sprawl only happens when ACLs are misconfigured
Granting a new narrow role feels safer in the moment than reusing a broader existing role, but without periodic review, that accumulated complexity itself becomes a security risk
questions.explain: Each individual decision to create a narrow role can be correct, yet the unreviewed accumulation over years becomes a risk independent of any single role's configuration.
